page: UpCloud DEV-2xCPU-4GB is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Developer family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9575F cores running at 2.0 GHz, with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 60 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector and cryptography extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests and top-tier single-threaded gzip compression. However, due to its shared CPU allocation and dual-core configuration, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks are significantly constrained. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation tests fall into the weak category (bottom 25%). Memory performance is also a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the poor category (bottom 10%), although cached read bandwidth remains average at 372.02 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a budget-friendly entry point for non-production environments, leveraging shared AMD EPYC resources to keep overhead low. The resource density is tailored for lightweight workloads rather than resource-intensive operations. It is best suited for software development, testing, basic web serving, and lightweight single-threaded tasks. It is not recommended for database operations, heavy multi-threaded processing, or memory-intensive applications due to documented performance degradation in those areas.
